chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from his brother Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Rabat, raising it, said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: If a Zimmi man (a Jew or Christian under protection) becomes a Muslim while his father is alive, and his father has other children besides him, then when the father dies, the Muslim son inherits all of his wealth, and his (other) children and his wife do not inherit anything along with the Muslim.

key_terms.ذِمِّيّاً: A non-Muslim subject living under Islamic protection

ai.seo_question: How does the conversion of a son to Islam affect the inheritance of his non-Muslim father according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the principle of 'Khulw' (exclusivity), where the convert's Islam acts as a barrier preventing non-Muslim kin from inheriting him, while he retains the right to inherit their estate. It highlights the Shia juristic view that religious affiliation is the primary determinant of inheritance rights in mixed-faith families, superseding blood ties with non-Muslims. This ruling underscores the spiritual and legal separation between the believer and the disbeliever in matters of worldly wealth distribution.
